competitors.name: Space Exploration Technologies Corp. (SpaceX; Starlink, Starlink Mobile direct-to-cell)
competitors.why: named first in ASTS 10-K Competition: Starlink LEO constellation competes in the direct-to-device segment for the same MNO partners and smartphone end users; owns its launch and, via the EchoStar AWS-4/H-block/AWS-3 purchase (FCC approved 2026-05-12, licenses in trust since 2026-05-22), its own mobile spectrum

competitors.name: Iridium Communications Inc.
competitors.why: named in ASTS 10-K Competition; LEO mobile satellite operator selling voice, IoT and government (DoD) service; competes with ASTS for U.S. Government satellite-communications contracts and for low-data-rate direct-to-device (NTN) messaging

competitors.name: Globalstar, Inc.
competitors.why: named in ASTS 10-K Competition; LEO MSS operator whose constellation and owned MSS spectrum carry satellite messaging to standard smartphones under a wholesale capacity arrangement with a large handset maker, i.e. a direct-to-device alternative for the same end users

competitors.name: Viasat, Inc. (owner of Inmarsat Global Limited)
competitors.why: ASTS 10-K names Inmarsat; Inmarsat is owned by Viasat, so Viasat's filings are the public numbers for it; GEO/L-band mobile satellite services for government, maritime and aviation and an announced direct-to-device effort

competitors.name: Skylo Technologies (private)
competitors.why: named in ASTS 10-K Competition; NB-NTN direct-to-device messaging over leased MSS spectrum on partner GEO satellites, sold through MNOs and handset makers

competitors.name: Thuraya Telecommunications Co. (part of Space42, Abu Dhabi)
competitors.why: named in ASTS 10-K Competition; regional GEO mobile satellite operator in EMEA/Asia, a regional alternative for MSS voice/data customers

notes: fd NAMED COMPETITORS (10-K Item 1, Competition, pf_10k_20260302): SpaceX's Starlink (direct-to-device LEO), Inmarsat Global Limited, Globalstar, Thuraya Telecommunications Co., Iridium Communications and Skylo; also regional GEO MSS operators, VSAT operators and, indirectly, terrestrial networks. ASTS positions itself as cellular broadband to unmodified handsets versus competitors' low data rate (SOS) services.

fd SECTOR POSITION: ASTS sells capacity wholesale to MNOs on a revenue-share basis (10-K Item 1: 'sell our services on a revenue share basis to MNOs'), plus gateway equipment and U.S. Government work (SDA $43.0m testing contract, SDA Europa Track 2 ~$30.0m, MDA SHIELD IDIQ; Q2 2026 release: >$125m of new U.S. Government awards). The revenue-share percentage is not disclosed (pf_10k_20260302, pf_10q_20260810, pf_rel_20260810_1).

fd SHARE: ASTS H1 2026 revenue $46.2m (products $37.8m + services $8.4m, pf_10q_20260810) against SpaceX Enterprise & Government revenue, which includes Starlink Mobile, of $5,042m in 9M 2026 (+70% y/y; Q3 $2,127m, +91%) (fd_10q_spcx_20260930). Starlink Mobile is not reported separately, so the direct-to-device share cannot be measured from filings; SpaceX is clearly ahead in commercial D2D service (T-Mobile service live) while ASTS is pre-service (beta planned 2026).

fd SHARE: legacy MSS competitors grow slowly: Iridium revenue +4.8% 9M 2026 with operating margin falling to 16.9% from 27.4% (fd_cf_irdm); Globalstar +6.0% H1 2026 at a 2.5% operating margin (fd_cf_gsat); Viasat/Inmarsat +2.7% FY to Mar-2026, -1.2% in the June 2026 quarter (fd_cf_vsat). None shows share loss to ASTS yet (ASTS has no service revenue); Iridium's margin drop is not attributed in this lane's sources.

fd COMPETITOR CONTEXT: SpaceX (SPCX) listed 2026-06-12 (FMP profile); its 10-Q for Q3 2026 states it is evaluating a potential combination with Tesla, Inc. with no assurance of an agreement (fd_10q_spcx_20260930). bottlenecks.reading: The scarce thing ASTS supplies is space-based cellular broadband capacity to standard unmodified smartphones using MNO low/mid-band spectrum (Block 1 demonstrated ~98.9 Mbps peak to a phone). Supply is set by satellites in orbit: 13 BlueBirds at 2026-08-10 against a 10-K plan of ~45-60 Block 2 by end-2026 and a 248-satellite FCC filing; BB17-46 are in production. Launch access and manufacturing cadence, not demand, gate ASTS's capacity through 2027; SpaceX adds capacity with its own launches and >11,100 Starlink broadband and mobile satellites.

Spectrum is the second bottleneck: ASTS relies on MNO spectrum leased under the FCC Supplemental Coverage from Space framework (Verizon, AT&T, FirstNet leases; FCC granted in part / deferred in part in Aug 2025), Ligado L-band and pending 2 GHz applications, targeting ~100 MHz in the U.S. and 60+ MHz globally. Its main competitor bought its own: SpaceX's purchase of EchoStar's 50 MHz AWS-4/H-block plus up to 15 MHz AWS-3 was FCC-approved 2026-05-12 and the licenses moved to a trust on 2026-05-22, removing SpaceX's dependence on a carrier's spectrum.

Paid adoption of the core service is not yet visible in ASTS's own numbers: the SpaceMobile service has generated no revenue; H1 2026 revenue was $37.8m of gateway products to MNOs plus $8.4m of mostly U.S. Government services; remaining performance obligations ~$1.2bn at 2026-06-30 with only ~6.6% expected within 12 months, and MNO revenue-share consideration is excluded as constrained. Management cites ~$1.30bn contracted backlog and 60+ MNO partners covering 3bn+ subscribers, which are commitments and logos, not paid usage.

Channel power: AT&T, T-Mobile and Verizon announced a joint venture on 2026-10-02 to pool resources for U.S. direct-to-device; AT&T and Verizon keep their ASTS deployments and T-Mobile its Starlink service. Whether the JV standardizes terms that lower the satellite operator's share, or channels pooled spectrum to ASTS, is not disclosed.

Hypothesis: a carrier JV that pools U.S. spectrum and negotiates jointly with satellite operators could raise ASTS's addressable spectrum but compress its revenue share versus bilateral deals; no term sheet is public.

Market direction is up but size is uncertain: Omdia (2026-03-02) projects smartphone satellite D2D service revenue of $11.99bn and 411m monthly active users by 2030 (revenue growth ~49% a year 2026-2030) and expects cellular-standard devices to exceed 95% of D2D MAUs, naming Starlink D2C and AST SpaceMobile as cellular-standard examples. This is one attributed study, a warning row on the size of the prize, not a driver.
